mantras.anvaya_en: Subject and verb: a speaker label.

comm.t: Medhas, the seer of the frame story (1.10), resumes his narrative to King Suratha and the merchant Samādhi. The sixth chapter follows directly on the end of the fifth, where the Devī sent Śumbha’s messenger back with her answer (5.128–129). In the Gita Press pāṭha this first mantra of the chapter carries the bīja ॐ, which belongs to the recitation, not to the Purāṇa.

sandhi.note: Final i before a dissimilar vowel becomes y: इति + आ → इत्या.
Before s the visarga may stay or be assimilated to s; the Gita Press keeps the visarga (देव्याः स, not देव्यास्स).
सः drops its visarga before the consonant d. दूतः before initial a becomes दूतो, and the a of अमर्ष- is absorbed into the o (avagraha).

samasa.sense: seething with resentment at the Devī’s refusal

samasa.literal: to the king of the daityas
samasa.sense: to Śumbha. At the end of a tatpuruṣa राजन् becomes the a-stem राज (a samāsānta suffix), hence the dative राजाय.

morph.note: Imperfect of सम् + आ + √चक्ष्: the augment a follows the prefixes and merges with आ (सम्-आ-अ-चष्ट); before the ending -त the k of the conjunct kṣ is lost and ṣ + t becomes ṣṭ (ष्टुना ष्टुः, 8.4.41).
Absolutive in -य (ल्यप्), the form taken when the verb has a prefix (आ). √कर्ण् ‘to ear, hear’ is a nominal verb from कर्ण ‘ear’.
Absolutive in -य of सम् + आ + √गम्. Grammar allows the nasal to stay or be lost before ल्यप्: समागम्य or समागत्य; the text has the first.

mantras.anvaya: देव्याः इति वचः आकर्ण्य अमर्षपूरितः सः दूतः समागम्य दैत्यराजाय विस्तरात् समाचष्ट।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two absolutives (आकर्ण्य, समागम्य) lead to the one finite verb समाचष्ट; the subject is सः दूतः with its predicate adjective अमर्षपूरितः.
mantras.lit: Having heard thus the words of the Devī, that messenger, filled with indignation, having come back, reported (them) in detail to the king of the daityas.
mantras.tr: When he had heard these words of the Devī, the messenger, seething with indignation, went back and told the king of the daityas everything at length.

comm.t: The messenger is Sugrīva (5.102). What he reports is the Devī’s vow — whoever conquers her in battle and matches her strength will be her husband (5.120) — and her invitation to Śumbha or Niśumbha to come and win her (5.121, 5.129). His anger is the anger of a servant whose master has been slighted.

The uttama-carita moves by escalation: after the messenger come Dhūmralocana (this chapter), Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa (chapter 7), Raktabīja (chapter 8), and finally Niśumbha and Śumbha themselves. Each refusal brings a stronger envoy.

morph.note: Nominative of the consonant stem राज् ‘king’ (as in सम्राट्): the final j becomes ṣ, then a stop at the end of the word, ṭ (राट्). The same stem gives असुरराजम्, असुरराजः in other cases.
प्र + आह: आह belongs to √ब्रू; grammar makes it a present form with perfect-type endings, but the epics and Purāṇas use it as the narrative past ‘(he) said’.

mantras.anvaya: ततः तस्य दूतस्य तत् वाक्यम् आकर्ण्य सक्रोधः असुरराट् दैत्यानाम् अधिपं धूम्रलोचनं प्राह।
mantras.anvaya_en: Absolutive clause (तस्य दूतस्य तत् वाक्यम् आकर्ण्य), subject with its predicate adjective (सक्रोधः असुरराट्), the person addressed (दैत्यानाम् अधिपं धूम्रलोचनम्), verb (प्राह).
mantras.lit: Having heard that report of that messenger, then the king of the asuras, in anger, said to the chief of the daityas, Dhūmralocana:
mantras.tr: When the lord of the asuras heard the messenger’s report, he flew into a rage and said to Dhūmralocana, a commander of the daityas:

comm.t: Śumbha does not answer the Devī’s challenge himself; he sends a commander. The chapter’s Gita Press colophon calls Dhūmralocana a general (सेनानी) of Śumbha and Niśumbha; his name means ‘he whose eyes are smoke-coloured’.
A modern reading, not a traditional one: the ‘smoke-eyed’ general is sent to seize what he cannot see clearly. The text itself says nothing of the name’s meaning.

samasa.sense: at the head of your own troops

samasa.type: tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa (instrumental of cause), containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa
samasa.literal: agitated by the dragging of the hair
samasa.sense: helpless and dishevelled from being hauled by the hair
samasa.alt: Also read with an ablative of cause, केशाकर्षणात् विह्वला (pañcamī tatpuruṣa); the sense is the same.

morph.note: Imperative of आ + √नी ‘lead towards’ = ‘bring’. The thematic stem नय- takes the bare stem as the 2nd singular imperative.
परिवारित is the past participle of the causative of परि + √वृ (वारय- + इत): ‘made to be surrounded’, i.e. ‘surrounded, escorted’.
Past participle of √दुष् ‘to be spoiled’, used as an adjective: ‘corrupt, wicked’. In Śumbha’s mouth an insult: ‘the insolent one’.

mantras.anvaya: हे धूम्रलोचन, स्वसैन्यपरिवारितः त्वम् आशु ताम् दुष्टाम् केशाकर्षणविह्वलाम् बलात् आनय।
mantras.anvaya_en: Vocative, subject with its participle phrase, the imperative आनय with its object ताम् दुष्टाम् and the predicate adjective केशाकर्षणविह्वलाम्; बलात् gives the manner.
mantras.lit: O Dhūmralocana, you, surrounded by your own army, bring quickly by force that wicked one, distraught from the dragging of her hair.
mantras.tr: Dhūmralocana, take your army and bring that insolent woman here at once — by force, dragged helpless by the hair.
mantras.tr_note: केशाकर्षणविह्वलाम् describes the state in which she is to arrive; the tr turns it into a phrase of manner.

comm.t: Śumbha takes up the threat his messenger had already made (5.126: केशाकर्षणनिर्धूतगौरवा, ‘your dignity shaken off by being dragged by the hair’). The phrase केशाकर्षणविह्वलाम् returns in Dhūmralocana’s mouth (6.9), and the order to drag her by the hair is repeated to Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa (6.23).

To drag a woman by the hair is, in the epic world, the sign of the worst outrage — it is what is done to Draupadī in the Mahābhārata’s assembly hall. By making it his order, Śumbha shows the listener what kind of power he is.

sandhi.note: Final t becomes d before the voiced y.
ā + u → o (वा + उत्- → वोत्-). Then the final e of उत्तिष्ठते absorbs the initial a of अपरः (avagraha).
सः loses its visarga before h. हन्तव्यः before a becomes हन्तव्यो with avagraha; अमरः before the voiced v becomes अमरो; वा + अपि → वापि. The same -aḥ → -o gives यक्षो गन्धर्व.
-aḥ before a vowel other than a: the visarga becomes y, the y is dropped, and the vowels stand apart.

samasa.vigraha: तस्याः परित्राणं ददाति इति (तत्परित्राणम् = तस्याः परित्राणम्)
samasa.type: upapada tatpuruṣa (द from √दा with the kṛt affix क), containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa
samasa.sense: anyone who takes her side and defends her. The pronoun stem तद् stands for the feminine (her) inside the compound.

morph.note: उद् + √स्था: the s of स्था is lost after उद् (उत्था-), and the present stem is तिष्ठ-. The ātmanepada is the one grammar prescribes for उद् + √स्था when it does not mean rising physically — ‘to come forward, make an effort’.
Gerundive (तव्यत्) of √हन्: ‘to be killed’. The agent, ‘by you’, is understood.
Indefinite pronoun: the interrogative किम् declined (कः) with the particle चित् — ‘someone, anyone’.

mantras.anvaya: यदि वा कश्चित् अपरः तत्परित्राणदः उत्तिष्ठते, सः अमरः वा अपि यक्षः गन्धर्वः एव वा (भवतु), (त्वया) हन्तव्यः।
mantras.anvaya_en: A conditional clause (यदि … उत्तिष्ठते) and its main clause (सः हन्तव्यः); the three classes of being (अमरः वा अपि यक्षः गन्धर्वः एव वा) say who the protector might be.
mantras.lit: And if any other, giving her protection, rises up — he is to be killed, whether he be an immortal, or even a yakṣa, or a gandharva.
mantras.tr: And if anyone else comes forward to protect her — god, yakṣa or gandharva — kill him.

comm.t: Śumbha imagines that the woman can only be defended by someone else — a god, a yakṣa, a gandharva — the very beings he has already conquered (5.86, 5.107–111). The protector who does rise up is her own lion (6.15), and the power he does not imagine is hers (6.13).
